study.title: Effect of acupuncture Baihui acupoint-Yintang acupoint-Neiguan acupoint combined with conventional Western medicine treatment on cerebral blood flow in insomnia patients: a 3D-ASL functional magnetic resonance imaging study
study.study_design: randomized controlled design; open-label trial without sham acupuncture
study.blinding: outcome assessors blinded; individuals responsible for collecting and analyzing fMRI data, as well as those scoring the PSQI and HAMA, were not involved in the treatment allocation process and were unaware of which group each patient belonged to; patients and acupuncturists not blinded
study.population: patients with insomnia admitted to Shenzhen Hospital of Beijing University of Chinese Medicine (Long Gang) from June 2021 to December 2022
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) Met the diagnostic criteria for primary insomnia, no depression, anxiety and other mental or psychological disorders; (2) Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) score >7; (3) Age > 18 years old; (4) No serious skin or blood-related diseases, such as neurodermatitis and atopic dermatitis, thrombocytopenia, coagulation disorders and hemophilia
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) Severe organic diseases such as liver and kidney dysfunction; (2) Unable to accept the treatment in this study, fainting and afraid of acupuncture, unable to cooperate with doctors to complete data collection before and after treatment; (3) There were contraindications of magnetic resonance (MR) scanning

arms.dropouts: 0 (follow-up n=50, analysis n=50 per CONSORT diagram)
0 (follow-up n=50, analysis n=50 per CONSORT diagram)

interventions.participant_instructions_exact: took alprazolam orally, with a dosage of 0.5–0.8 mg each time, 30 min before going to bed
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: conventional Western medicine treatment for insomnia

interventions.procedure_label_exact: acupuncture treatment (Baihui acupoint-Yintang acupoint-Neiguan acupoint) combined with alprazolam
interventions.manipulation_exact: electric acupuncture using the Yingdi pulse acupuncture therapy instrument; continuous-wave stimulation
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: intensity was adjusted to a level that elicited a mild but noticeable deqi sensation (a characteristic sensation of acupuncture, often described as a dull ache, numbness, or tingling) in the patients without causing any discomfort or pain
interventions.electrical_intensity_exact: adjusted to a level that elicited a mild but noticeable deqi sensation without causing any discomfort or pain
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: once a day for a total of 28 days
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: licensed practitioners with a minimum of 5 years of clinical experience in acupuncture; undergone formal training in traditional Chinese medicine acupuncture techniques and had also received specific training on the use of acupuncture therapy instrument; all acupuncturists participated in a standardized training session prior to the start of the study
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: acupuncture points have a clear effect on the treatment of insomnia; Baihui acupoint-Yintang acupoint-Neiguan acupoint combined with conventional Western medicine treatment

sensory_interoceptive_responses.item_or_subscale_exact: deqi sensation (dull ache, numbness, or tingling)
sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: mild but noticeable deqi sensation (a characteristic sensation of acupuncture, often described as a dull ache, numbness, or tingling) in the patients without causing any discomfort or pain
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Deqi was described as a target/intended sensation; no quantitative deqi measurement instrument was used; no deqi scores reported

neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 30 layers of continuous scanning to cover the whole brain
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian filter with a full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of 6 mm
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: exceeding 2 mm of translation in any of the three axes (x, y, z) or 2 degrees of rotation around any of the three axes (pitch, roll, yaw)
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: average cerebral blood flow (CBF) value (mL/100 g/min)

additional_acquisition_parameters.ASL_labeling_scheme_exact: pulsed arterial spin-labeling (PASL) approach; arterial blood water is magnetically labeled by a short radiofrequency pulse applied to a selected slice in the neck region

neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_steps_exact: image realignment using rigid-body transformation algorithm to correct for head motion artifacts; spatial normalization to MNI template using non-linear registration algorithm; smoothing with Gaussian filter FWHM 6 mm

extraction_notes.note: No exact mean ± SD values for PSQI or HAMA scores at any timepoint are reported in the text. Values are only visible in Figures 3 and 4 as bar charts, which cannot be read precisely from the PDF. These are noted as 'not_reported' in the clinical outcomes fields.
No exact mean ± SD CBF values for any ROI at any timepoint are reported in the text. Values are shown only in Figure 2 as bar charts, which cannot be read precisely from the PDF.
No MNI or Talairach coordinates are reported for any neural result. All neuroimaging results are reported as ROI-level CBF averages without coordinate tables.
No adverse events section or mention of adverse events is included in the paper. It is unclear whether adverse events were monitored or whether none occurred.

The paper does not report the sample size used for the neuroimaging analysis separately from the clinical analysis. It is inferred that all 100 randomized patients underwent fMRI, but this is not explicitly confirmed for each individual ROI analysis.

The voxel size is not explicitly reported in the methods section. FOV is listed as 25 mm × 25 mm (likely 250 mm × 250 mm given scanner context) and matrix 512 × 512 — however the paper states exactly '25 mm × 25 mm' for FOV which may be a reporting error or OCR artifact.

The paper states '95% CI' values for all comparisons, but these CIs appear to represent the mean difference between groups or within-group change rather than confidence intervals around a mean. The negative signs in CIs (e.g., −17.25 to −14.89) are preserved as reported.

The within-group CBF CI values (e.g., −6.433 to −4.067 for cerebellar cortex) are attributed to 'both groups' combined in the text; it is ambiguous whether these CIs apply to each group separately or to a pooled within-group estimate.

The paper states the study used '3D-ASL' but then describes a 'pulsed arterial spin-labeling (PASL) approach' in the methods — these are distinct ASL techniques. This internal inconsistency is preserved as reported.
No deqi quantification instrument (e.g., MASS, SASI, VAS) was used. Deqi was only described qualitatively as a target sensation for intensity titration. No deqi scores are reported.
No expectancy, credibility, or treatment blinding success measures were collected from participants. Authors acknowledge lack of strict blinding as a limitation.
No sham acupuncture control arm was included. The paper explicitly states 'This was an open-label trial without sham acupuncture.'
The paper does not prospectively report trial registration. Authors acknowledge: 'our study did not prospectively register.'
The needle type, needle size, insertion depth, and needle retention time for the acupuncture procedure are not reported.

The paper states CBF values were calculated for 'the left and right sides of each ROI' but all reported results are presented as single average values without hemisphere-specific breakdowns. It is unclear whether laterality differences were analyzed.

The study group received both electroacupuncture AND alprazolam, while the control group received only alprazolam. Therefore, the between-group difference reflects the combined effect of acupuncture add-on, not acupuncture alone. This is correctly characterized in the paper but relevant for meta-analysis interpretation.
The specific software used for preprocessing (realignment, normalization, smoothing) is not reported; only the analysis software 'Functool-ASL graphics processing software' is named.
CBF bar chart values in Figure 2 and PSQI/HAMA bar chart values in Figures 3 and 4 are the primary data presentation; exact numeric values cannot be reliably extracted from the PDF bar charts.
